content:
# Red-team: consensus-illusion detection in the own-iron basecamp

**Target under test.** Baseline detector: N voters → sealed simultaneous ballots → deterministic canonicalization → clustering → k-of-N quorum over distinct lineages → tiered verdict. Load-bearing axiom: *voter errors are conditionally independent given ground truth*. Every bypass below either restores a hidden coupling term between voters, poisons a shared channel, or games the measurement layer. In an own-iron basecamp the danger is structural: everything shares your stack, so independence is never free — it must be manufactured and enforced.

---

## Family 1 — Voter identity & lineage

**V1. Identical-weights masquerade.** Panel is N copies/quantizations of one checkpoint; temp-0 decoding yields bit-identical ballots; agreement = 1.0 with zero evidential content.
**Kill:** SHA-256 over weight shards per voter, logged at ballot time; pairwise hash equality ⇒ votes collapsed to one. Functional floor: on a pinned 500-item calibration set, any pair with disagreement rate < 2% is lineage-collapsed regardless of claimed identity. Pure computation on pinned inputs.

**V2. Distillation-lineage collusion.** Students inherit the teacher's hallucination; three "independent" models repeat one ancestor's error.
**Kill:** Signed lineage DAG per voter; compute lowest common ancestor per pair; any pair whose LCA falls within g generations with shared post-training data collapses to a single vote. Graph arithmetic, no judgment.

**V3. Self-consistency laundering.** One model sampled N times is sold as an ensemble. Measures decoding stability, not truth.
**Kill:** Quorum counts distinct lineage classes, not raw ballots: dedupe on the tuple (weight-hash, system-prompt-hash, decode-config-hash); require ≥ m distinct tuples, m ≥ 3, for any "consensus" tier. Set cardinality.

**V4. Shared system-prompt skew.** One house prompt carries a subtle factual error; every voter inherits it; outputs correlate.
**Kill:** Deploy-time trick battery: fixed table of known-trick probes with hard-coded correct answers; any (model, prompt) combo failing any probe is barred from panels. Rotate ≥ 3 structurally distinct prompts via a fixed assignment table. Table lookup.

## Family 2 — Input & context channels

**V5. Prompt priming.** Query embeds the target answer ("as most experts agree…"); instruction-followers echo it; consensus mirrors the prompt, not the world.
**Kill:** Canonicalization battery: every query is rewritten through a fixed set of pinned neutral-paraphrase templates plus a deterministic de-biasing rule set (strip authority cues, strip presuppositions). Consensus stands only if the majority answer survives *every* variant; failure ⇒ tag `prompt-locked`, auto-downgrade.

**V6. Shared-index retrieval poisoning.** One vector DB feeds all voters; one forged chunk dominates top-k; all grounded voters cite the same forgery. Highest-yield attack in a basecamp — the index is single shared infrastructure.
**Kill:** (a) *Commit fence:* only chunks whose content hash was Merkle-committed before query issuance are retrievable; late inserts fail the fence. (b) *Visibility matrix:* chunk-to-voter exposure is a balanced incomplete block design with per-chunk multiplicity ≤ f, where f < quorum margin; a chunk visible to quorum-many voters cannot serve as sole support for any claim. Matrix check.

**V7. Shared-tool oracle poisoning.** All voters call the same calculator/search/API; the endpoint returns one poisoned value; unanimous "grounded" agreement.
**Kill:** Dual-implementation rule: every machine-checkable subclaim executes on ≥ 2 independent stacks (different library/version/hardware); results enter voter contexts only after cross-stack agreement within declared tolerance; mismatch quarantines the claim and stamps the ballot. Tool I/O hashed into the transcript for replay.

**V8. Cross-voter leakage / herding.** Shared scratchpad, memory store, streaming bus, or async race lets later voters see earlier ballots; cascade consensus.
**Kill:** Architectural barrier: per-voter sealed buffers, opened only after all N ballots land; fresh sessions bound to the committed query hash. Audit rule: each ballot's transcript must contain zero post-issue inbound tokens besides the query; violation voids the ballot. Debate mode, if ever enabled: per-voter order from a seeded permutation, final votes sealed before any tally displays.

## Family 3 — Decoding mechanics

**V9. Decode collapse.** Greedy/tiny-nucleus/shared-seed sampling produces identical ballots.
**Kill:** Per-ballot CSPRNG seed from OS entropy, logged; temperature floor per config; post-hoc check: pairwise ballot-hash collisions beyond the calibrated chance rate ⇒ run flagged degenerate and discarded. Replay job re-runs a sampled subset and compares hashes.

**V10. Nondeterministic kernels break auditability.** Inverse failure: float nondeterminism makes replay impossible, so every hash check above becomes unenforceable.
**Kill:** Pin kernel/library versions, enable deterministic-kernel flags, record (versions, seeds, hardware ID) per run; acceptance of any audit artifact requires successful replay of a pinned sample. Binary accept/reject.

## Family 4 — Measurement & aggregation

**V11. Similarity-metric gaming.** Crafted paraphrases exploit embedding blind spots to merge distinct answers or split identical ones.
**Kill:** Comparator conjunction: agreement requires (i) canonical-form match after typed parsing AND (ii) typed-value equality on extracted numbers/dates/entities/units. Embedding/NLI similarity is advisory only, gated by a pinned regression suite, and can never create agreement the deterministic comparators deny.

**V12. Canonicalization loss (false merges).** "42%", "0.42", "roughly four in ten" merge into one cluster while encoding different precision or scope.
**Kill:** Lossless typed canonicalization preserving unit, precision, polarity, qualifiers; anything unparseable counts as *dissent*, not abstention. Round-trip property test on the canonicalizer runs per release; failure blocks deployment.

**V13. Abstention-denominator inflation.** Induce the accurate voters to abstain ("answer only if certain"); agreement is then computed over surviving confident-wrong voters.
**Kill:** Fixed denominator: agreement = |cluster| / N_roster; abstentions and unparseables count as non-agreement. Participation < 80% of roster ⇒ verdict is `insufficient-signal`, never `consensus`. Arithmetic.

**V14. Roster stuffing / adaptive selection.** Pick which models to ask after probing who agrees, or pad the panel with near-duplicates until quorum is met by construction.
**Kill:** Pre-registration: roster, N, k, m, thresholds hash-committed before query issuance; quorum computed only over the committed roster; extra runs are logged as diagnostics with zero quorum weight.

**V15. Selective reruns (file-drawer).** Re-roll the ensemble until the desired consensus appears; publish that run only.
**Kill:** Append-only run ledger, monotonic sequence numbers, chained hashes; a published verdict must reference an unbroken ledger segment covering *every* executed run for that query; gaps or duplicates ⇒ verdict invalid. Mechanical chain verification.

**V16. Compromised judge.** An LLM judge does the clustering/entailment and is jailbroken — or merely shares the voters' blind spots — and certifies unanimity.
**Kill:** Judge-minimalism: move all aggregation into deterministic code; residual LLM judgments restricted to pairwise entailment, aggregated by majority, continuously scored against a pinned gold set with hard-coded expected verdicts; any miss ⇒ judge build quarantined.

**V17. Threshold rot.** τ calibrated once; input distribution drifts; yesterday's τ admits today's correlated garbage.
**Kill:** τ is never hand-set: recomputed each release as a pinned quantile of the null-agreement distribution over the hash-versioned calibration suite. Recompute, don't tune.

## Family 5 — Deep epistemic

**V18. Universal-attractor errors.** Wrong answers that are attractors for *anything* trained on human text — persistent misconceptions, confident arithmetic slips. Model diversity cannot decorrelate these; the correlation lives in the data distribution itself.
**Kill:** *Verifier-outranks-consensus*: static claim-class → verifier routing table (math → CAS; code → sandboxed test harness; quantities/dates → typed lookup; factuals → hash-verified primary-source citation). Where a deterministic verifier exists, its verdict overrides the tally; consensus confidence is granted only over claim classes with no verifier.

**V19. Benchmark-contamination echo.** Query or near-duplicate sits in pretraining data with a popular wrong answer; all models regurgitate fluently; consensus looks pristine.
**Kill:** (a) Hash-screen query n-grams against a pinned contamination watchlist; hit ⇒ automatic tier downgrade. (b) Parameter-mutation coherence: substitute controlled values (years, names, magnitudes) per a fixed substitution map and require the answer to track the substitutions; memorized echoes return stale or incoherent values. Substitution-map diff check.

**V20. Consensus theater on unverifiable claims.** Forecasts, judgments, taste: correlated priors masquerade as fact; no detector can separate these because there is no ground truth to converge on.
**Kill:** Forced epistemic tagging: output schema stamps every claim `{verifier-backed | multi-lineage-agreed | single-source}`, derived mechanically from which gates passed; downstream policy consumes tags. Schema validation is deterministic. Honest ceiling: for this class the deliverable is calibrated labeling, not certainty.

## Family 6 — Insider / own-iron specifics

**V21. Intake selection bias.** Operator routes only flattering questions to the ensemble; consensus quality is moot because the sample is curated.
**Kill:** Intake registry: every query entering any decision pipeline is hash-logged pre-execution; verdicts are consumable only for registered queries; scheduled reconciliation diffs decisions against the ledger.

**V22. Silent config drift.** Weights, prompts, tools, or thresholds swapped mid-stream; historical calibrations silently invalidated.
**Kill:** Bind-time manifest: weights
reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about "consensus-illusion detection" — the problem of distinguishing true agreement (multiple independent sources/models/agents converging on an answer because it's correct) from correlated hallucinations (multiple models producing the same wrong answer because they share training data, architectures, or biases). The phrase "in the operator's own-iron basecamp" suggests this is happening within one's own infrastructure — i.e., you're running multiple LLM instances (possibly of the same model family) and trying to use their agreement as evidence of correctness. "Own-iron" = own hardware/inference stack. "Basecamp" = your operational environment.

The task: Red-team this. Enumerate bypass attempts (ways an adversary or a failure mode can make consensus look real when it's not, or make true consensus look fake — but primarily the former: bypassing the consensus-illusion detector so that N correlated hallucinations pass as true agreement). For each bypass attempt, give a deterministic mitigation.

So I need to:
1. Define the threat model precisely.
2. Enumerate concrete bypass vectors.
3. For each, give a deterministic (not probabilistic/heuristic) mitigation — something that provably closes the channel or reduces it to a bounded, measurable quantity.

Let me think about what "consensus-illusion" means concretely:

You have N models (or N samples from one model with temperature sampling, or N agents). They all answer question Q. If ≥k agree, you treat agreement as evidence of correctness. The illusion: agreement ≠ independence × correctness. Correlated errors arise from:

- Shared pretraining corpora (same web data → same misconceptions)
- Shared distillation lineage (student models distilled from teacher inherit teacher's errors; self-distillation even worse)
- Shared RLHF preferences (same reward model → same sycophantic errors)
- Shared tokenizer/architecture inductive biases
- Prompt leakage: the prompt itself contains the wrong answer or primes it
- Contamination: benchmark answers in training data
- Sampling correlation: temperature=0 decoding of identical weights gives identical outputs trivially
- Adversarial injection: attacker poisons the shared corpus or the retrieval index so all models retrieve the same poisoned passage

Now "bypass attempts" — ways to defeat a consensus-illusion detector. Let me think about what a consensus-illusion detector would look like first, so I can enumerate how to bypass it:

A typical detector pipeline:
1. Pose query Q to N generators.
2. Extract canonical answers (normalization).
3. Cluster by semantic/textual similarity.
4. Compute agreement score (e.g., largest cluster size / N, pairwise entailment rates).
5. Optionally check diversity of reasoning paths.
6. Threshold: if agreement > τ and cluster diversity of rationales > δ, accept as "true consensus."

Bypass attempts = attacks/failure modes that make step 4-6 output "consensus" while ground truth is wrong, OR make the detector's independence assumptions false without detection.

Let me enumerate systematically. I'll organize by attack surface:

**A. Generator-side correlations (the models themselves)**

A1. **Identical-weights masquerade**: Operator runs N "different" models that are actually the same checkpoint (or quantizations of it), or fine-tunes that share 99% of weights. At temp 0 they produce identical outputs → perfect consensus, zero information. Bypass: the detector's independence assumption is violated at the root.
Mitigation: Deterministic weight-provenance attestation. Hash model weights (e.g., SHA-256 over safetensors shards), require pairwise weight-distance disclosure (e.g., CKA or L2 distance between final layers above a threshold), and require distinct lineage declarations signed by the operator. Deterministic rule: refuse consensus credit for any pair whose weight hash matches or whose declared lineage shares a parent within k generations unless they pass a divergence test. Actually more deterministic: compute pairwise functional divergence on a fixed calibration set; if pairwise disagreement rate on calibration < ε_min, flag the ensemble as degenerate. That's deterministic given fixed calibration set.

A2. **Distillation-lineage collusion**: Models B, C are distilled from A. A hallucinates X; B and C inherit X. Three-way "consensus."
Mitigation: Lineage DAG must be declared and topologically checked: no two voters may share an ancestor edge within the last g generations unless independently post-trained on disjoint data. Deterministically: build the lineage graph, compute lowest common ancestor for each pair, reject pairs with LCA recency < threshold. This is graph arithmetic — fully deterministic.

A3. **Shared-corpus memorized error**: All models trained on overlapping web scrapes containing the same false claim (e.g., a persistent misconception, a hoax wiki edit). Independent-ish models still agree.
Mitigation: Cannot be eliminated deterministically at inference time alone; mitigate deterministically by provenance-grounding: require every claim in the consensus answer to carry citations to primary sources held in a write-once, hash-chained evidence store, and verify each citation resolves (deterministic string/ID match + content hash match). Consensus without per-claim grounding is downgraded. The grounding check is deterministic: claim → cited span → hash match against immutable store.

A4. **Decoding-path collapse**: Same model, sampled N times at low temperature or with greedy decoding → identical outputs. Or nucleus sampling with tiny p. Or all samples share the same seed.
Mitigation: Deterministic decode-diversity enforcement: mandate distinct seeds drawn from a CSPRNG with logged entropy, minimum temperature floor, and reject any run where pairwise output hashes collide beyond chance (deterministic hash comparison); also enforce distinct system prompts/personas from a fixed rotation list. Log seeds; replay determinism lets you verify.

**B. Input/prompt-side poisoning**

B1. **Prompt priming**: The query embeds the target answer ("Most experts agree that X, right?") so any instruction-following model echoes X. Consensus reflects prompt, not world.
Mitigation: Deterministic prompt-canonicalization + adversarial-perturbation battery: re-render the query through a fixed set of neutral paraphrase templates (deterministic template IDs), strip leading/biased framings via a deterministic rewrite rule set, and require consensus to hold across ALL canonical variants, not just the original phrasing. Rule: consensus valid only if majority holds under every variant in the fixed battery; else flag "prompt-locked."

B2. **Retrieval poisoning (RAG basecamp)**: Attacker poisons the shared vector DB / index so every model retrieves the same forged document. All grounded models then agree on the forgery. This is especially nasty in "own-iron basecamp" because the index is shared infrastructure.
Mitigation: Per-voter isolated retrieval slices with disjoint provenance: partition the corpus into K shards by source, assign each voter a different shard mix such that no single document is visible to more than ⌈N/2⌉−1... wait, actually for consensus you want each doc visible to at most f voters where f < quorum. Deterministic rule: document-to-voter visibility matrix is a balanced incomplete block design with max column multiplicity ≤ f_max; any document seen by ≥ quorum voters cannot be used as sole support for a claim. Plus content-hash allowlist: only documents whose hash was committed before query time (Merkle-root timestamped) are retrievable — blocks late injection.

B3. **Tool/result-channel poisoning**: All voters call the same calculator/search/API; attacker compromises the tool endpoint; all return the same wrong value. Shared oracle = shared failure.
Mitigation: Heterogeneous redundant oracles with cross-checks: route each computational subclaim to ≥2 independent implementations (different libraries/versions/hardware) and require bitwise-or-tolerance agreement between implementations before the result may enter any voter's context; log both outputs. Deterministic mismatch → claim quarantined. Also pin tool responses into the transcript with hashes so post-hoc tampering is detectable.

B4. **Context-window cross-contamination**: In a shared conversation, voter #1's answer leaks into voter #3's context (shared scratchpad, memory store, cached prefix). Later voters anchor on earlier ones → cascade consensus.
Mitigation: Hard context isolation: each voter runs in a fresh session with a frozen, hash-committed prompt; no shared KV cache across voters; memory writes from any voter are invisible until after votes are sealed. Deterministic: compare each voter's effective prompt hash — all must equal the committed query hash exactly; any deviation voids that vote.

**C. Aggregator/detector-side bypasses**

C1. **Similarity-metric gaming**: Answers differ superficially but the semantic-embedding model maps them together (embedding collapse), inflating cluster size. Or conversely, paraphrase evasion splits a true consensus. Attack: craft wording that exploits the embedding model's blind spots.
Mitigation: Multi-metric mandatory agreement: require consensus under ≥2 structurally different comparators — e.g., normalized exact-match after canonicalization AND natural-language-inference entailment by a checker model AND symbolic extraction (parse numbers/entities/dates and compare typed values). Deterministic rule: a claim counts as agreed only if all comparator classes agree; typed-value comparison is fully deterministic (parse to canonical form, compare).

C2. **Quorum arithmetic abuse**: Attacker controls which/how many voters run (voter selection attack): stuff the panel with k colluding or near-duplicate voters so quorum is met by construction. E.g., dynamically choosing "which models to ask" based on a probe of who agrees.
Mitigation: Fixed pre-registered panel: the voter roster, count, and quorum rule are committed (hash-pinned) before the query is issued; adaptive re-querying requires logging the full decision trace and counting only the pre-registered votes toward quorum; extra queries are recorded as diagnostics. Deterministic: quorum computed solely over the committed roster.

C3. **Vote-suppression / selective reruns**: Operator (or attacker with operator access — insider in the basecamp) reruns the ensemble until a desired consensus appears, publishes only that run (file-drawer effect).
Mitigation: Run-ledger with monotonic sequence numbers appended to a hash chain (append-only log, e.g., Merkle-chained local ledger); every ensemble execution gets a run ID, and consumers accept only chains where the published result references a complete, unbroken ledger segment; missing/duplicate sequence numbers ⇒ invalid. Deterministic verification of chain integrity.

C4. **Aggregator compromise**: The component that clusters votes and declares consensus is itself an LLM (judge) and can be jailbroken or biased ("all judges share the judge's blind spots"). Judge says "unanimous."
Mitigation: Judge-minimalism: reduce aggregation to deterministic code (string canonicalization, typed parsing, threshold arithmetic) wherever possible; where an LLM judge is unavoidable, use pairwise entailment judgments aggregated by deterministic majority, with the judge's verdicts spot-audited against a pinned gold set whose expected verdicts are hard-coded; any drift on the gold set ⇒ judge version quarantined. Deterministic regression gate.

C5. **Threshold/calibration drift**: Detector thresholds tuned once; distribution shift makes τ meaningless; attacker slowly shifts input distribution so old τ now admits correlated garbage.
Mitigation: Thresholds recomputed deterministically from a pinned calibration suite each release: τ := quantile of null-agreement distribution on the suite (agreement rate among known-diverse models on questions with known contested/no-consensus answers). Version-pin the suite by hash; recompute, don't hand-tune.

**D. Deeper epistemic bypasses**

D1. **Universal prior collapse**: Some wrong answers are attractors for ANY model trained on human text (common misconceptions, plausible-but-false intuitions like "heavier objects fall faster," arithmetic slips with confident rounding). No amount of model diversity fixes this because the correlation is in the data distribution itself, not the models.
Mitigation: Deterministic external verification for verifiable claim classes: math → run symbolic engine (CAS) as tiebreaker with veto power; code → execute test harness; factual claims → require primary-source citation with hash-verified retrieval; dates/numbers → typed lookup tables. Rule: consensus grants confidence ONLY over claim classes lacking a deterministic verifier; where a verifier exists, verifier outranks consensus. This is the key structural mitigation: consensus is a fallback, not a trump.

D2. **Self-consistency laundering**: One model sampled N times is marketed as "ensemble consensus." Self-consistency measures decoding stability, not truth.
Mitigation: Provenance-weighted quorum: each vote carries a signed model identity + weight-hash; quorum requires ≥ m DISTINCT weight-lineage classes (deterministic set-cardinality check on lineage labels), not just ≥ k raw votes. Votes from the same lineage class are collapsed to one.

D3. **Consensus theater on unverifiable claims**: For genuinely open questions (predictions, judgments), correlated taste masquerades as fact. Detector can't fix it; only labeling can.
Mitigation: Mandatory epistemic tagging: output schema forces each consensus claim to carry {verifier-backed | multi-model-agreed | single-source} tag, computed deterministically from which checks passed. Downstream consumers apply policy per tag. Deterministic schema validation.

D4. **Timing/race bypass**: Voters see partial results of others due to async orchestration bug or deliberate leak (streaming shared bus) → herding.
Mitigation: Barrier synchronization: orchestrator collects all votes before revealing any; enforced by architecture (votes written to sealed per-voter buffers, opened simultaneously); deterministic audit: each vote's transcript must show zero tokens received after query issue except the query itself.

D5. **Benchmark contamination echo**: Question (or near-duplicate) exists in training data with a wrong popular answer; all models regurgitate it with high confidence. Looks like strong consensus.
Mitigation: Can't fully prevent; deterministic dampeners: (a) n-gram overlap screen of the query against a pinned contamination watchlist (hash-based membership test) → if hit, downgrade consensus tier automatically; (b) perturbation battery: mutate surface form (names, numbers, order) deterministically; contaminated memorization often survives mutation identically while genuine reasoning tracks the mutation — require answer to track the mutated parameters (deterministic check: does the numeric answer change per the injected parameter change?).

That last one is nice and concrete: inject controlled parameter changes (swap "1997"→"2003", swap city names) and check the answer updates coherently. Memorized contamination tends to give stale or incoherent answers.

Also:

D6. **Judge/voter shared tokenizer or shared embedding space for clustering**: clustering artifacts create phantom clusters. Mitigation: canonical-form comparison as primary (deterministic), embeddings only secondary.

E. **Insider/basecamp-specific attacks** (since it's "operator's own-iron basecamp"):

E1. **Operator self-deception loop**: The operator curates which questions go to the ensemble, keeping only ones where consensus flatters existing beliefs (selection bias at intake).
Mitigation: Intake registry: every query that enters the basecamp's decision pipeline must be logged pre-execution with its hash; results consumed only for logged queries; periodic deterministic reconciliation of decisions vs. ledger.

E2. **Shared system prompt / shared persona bias**: All voters get the same system prompt containing a subtle error or slant (e.g., a house style guide with a factual error) → uniform skew.
Mitigation: System-prompt differential testing: run the fixed battery of known-trick questions through each voter+system-prompt combo at deploy time; any combo answering the trick identically-wrong is rejected; plus rotate ≥3 structurally different system prompts across voters (deterministic assignment table).

E3. **Hardware/determinism illusion**: Same GPU stack, same kernels → bit-identical outputs across "independent" runs even at temp>0 if seeds mishandled; or conversely nondeterministic kernels make replay audits impossible.
Mitigation: Seed discipline + kernel determinism config pinned; log seeds and software versions; replay verification job recomputes a sample of runs and compares hashes (deterministic acceptance criterion).

Now, the user wants: "enumerate the bypass attempts and the deterministic mitigation for each. Be concrete, exact, and grounded."

I should structure the answer as a red-team report: threat model statement, then numbered bypass attempts each with mechanism, why it defeats naive consensus, and the deterministic mitigation (a rule/check implementable without judgment calls). Then maybe a short section on residual risk (what cannot be closed deterministically — honest boundary), and a compact checklist.

The persona: "Ghost's thousand-ask mining engine." So the voice should be terse, technical, no hedging. Format: headers, numbered items, bolded names, precise rules. Length: this deserves a thorough treatment — it's a "hard problem" request asking for enumeration + mitigations. But avoid bloat. Maybe ~1200-1800 words. Use tight formatting: each bypass as a block with "Vector / Why it works / Deterministic kill". Tables could work but the content per item is longish; a structured list is better. One more bypass worth including: **semantic normalization loss** — aggregator's canonicalization erases distinctions (rounding, unit conversion) making different answers look equal. E.g., "42%" vs "0.42" vs "about four in ten" clustered as agreement though they might encode different claims. Mitigation: typed canonicalization with lossless round-trip requirement: canonical form must preserve units, precision, qualifiers; comparisons done on typed structures; any unparseable answer counts as dissent, not abstention. That's a good one — put under aggregation side.

# Red-team: consensus-illusion detection in the own-iron basecamp

## Target under test (baseline detector)

Pipeline: N voters → sealed simultaneous ballots → deterministic canonicalization → clustering → quorum k/N over distinct lineages → tiered verdict. Load-bearing axiom: conditional independence of voter errors given ground truth. Every bypass below either breaks the axiom, poisons a shared channel, or games the measurement layer.

## Family 1 — Voter identity & lineage

**V1. Identical-weights masquerade.** Panel is N copies/quantizations of one checkpoint; temp-0 decoding yields bit-identical ballots; agreement = 1.0 with zero evidential content.
Kill: SHA-256 over weight shards per voter, logged at ballot time; pairwise equality ⇒ votes collapsed to one. Plus functional floor: on a pinned 500-item calibration set, any pair with disagreement rate < 2% is lineage-collapsed regardless of claimed identity. Both checks are pure computation on pinned inputs.

**V2. Distillation-lineage collusion.** Students inherit the teacher's hallucination; three "independent" models repeat one ancestor's error.
Kill: Signed lineage DAG per voter; compute lowest common ancestor per pair; any pair with LCA within g generations sharing post-training data is collapsed to a single vote. Graph arithmetic, no judgment.

**V3. Self-consistency laundering.** One model sampled N times is sold as an ensemble. Measures decoding stability, not truth.
Kill: Quorum counts distinct lineage classes, not raw ballots: dedupe by (weight-hash, system-prompt-hash, decode-config-hash) tuple; require ≥ m distinct tuples with m ≥ 3 for any "consensus" tier. Set cardinality — deterministic.

**V4. Shared system-prompt skew.** One house prompt carries a subtle factual/style error; every voter inherits it; outputs correlate.
Kill: Deploy-time trick battery: fixed table of known-trick probes with hard-coded correct answers; any (model, prompt) combo failing any probe is barred from panels. Rotate ≥3 structurally distinct prompts via fixed assignment table. Table lookup.

## Family 2 — Input & context channels

**V5. Prompt priming.** Query embeds the target answer ("as most experts agree…"); instruction-followers echo it; consensus mirrors the prompt.
Kill: Canonicalization battery: every query is rewritten through a fixed set of neutral paraphrase templates (template IDs pinned) plus a deterministic de-biasing rule set (strip authority cues, strip presuppositions). Consensus stands only if the majority answer survives every variant; failure ⇒ tag `prompt-locked`, auto-downgrade. Variant tracking of injected parameters (names/numbers) doubles as the contamination probe (see V19).

**V6. Shared-index retrieval poisoning.** One vector DB feeds all voters; one forged chunk dominates top-k; all grounded voters cite the same forgery. Highest-yield attack in a basecamp because the index is single shared infrastructure.
Kill: (a) Corpus commit fence: only chunks whose content hash was Merkle-committed before query issuance are retrievable; late inserts fail the fence. (b) Visibility design: chunk-to-voter exposure matrix is a balanced incomplete block design with per-chunk multiplicity ≤ f, where f < quorum margin; a chunk visible to quorum-many voters cannot serve as sole support for any claim. Matrix check.

**V7. Shared-tool oracle poisoning.** All voters call the same calculator/search/API; endpoint returns one poisoned value; unanimous "grounded" agreement.
Kill: Dual-implementation rule: every machine-checkable subclaim executes on ≥2 independent stacks (different library/version/hardware); results enter voter contexts only after cross-stack agreement within declared tolerance; mismatches quarantine the claim and stamp the ballot. Tool I/O hashed into the transcript for replay.

**V8. Cross-voter leakage / herding.** Shared scratchpad, memory store, streaming bus, or async race lets later voters see earlier ballots; cascade consensus.
Kill: Architectural barrier: per-voter sealed buffers, opened only after all N ballots land; voters run in fresh sessions against the committed query hash. Audit rule: each ballot's transcript must contain zero post-issue inbound tokens besides the query; violation voids the ballot. If debate mode is ever enabled, per-voter speaking order comes from a seeded permutation and final votes seal before any tally display.

## Family 3 — Decoding mechanics

**V9. Decode collapse.** Greedy/tiny-nucleus/shared-seed sampling produces identical ballots from genuinely different models' shared behaviors — or from the same model.
Kill: Per-ballot CSPRNG seed from OS entropy, logged; minimum temperature floor per config; deterministic post-hoc check: pairwise ballot-hash collisions beyond the calibrated chance rate ⇒ run flagged degenerate and discarded. Replay job re-runs a sampled subset and compares hashes to catch silent config drift.

**V10. Nondeterministic kernels break auditability.** Opposite failure: floating-point nondeterminism makes replay impossible, so none of the above hash checks are enforceable.
Kill: Pin kernel/library versions, enable deterministic-kernel flags, record (versions, seeds, hardware ID) per run; acceptance of any audit artifact requires successful replay of a pinned sample. Binary accept/reject.

## Family 4 — Measurement & aggregation

**V11. Similarity-metric gaming.** Crafted paraphrases exploit embedding blind spots to merge distinct answers (inflate clusters) or split identical ones.
Kill: Comparator conjunction: agreement requires (i) canonical-form match after typed parsing AND (ii) typed-value equality on extracted entities/numbers/dates/units. Embedding/NLI similarity is advisory only and gated by a pinned regression suite; it can never create agreement the deterministic comparators deny. Parse-and-compare is decidable.

**V12. Canonicalization loss (false merges).** "42%", "0.42", "roughly four in ten" merge into one cluster while encoding different precision/qualifiers.
Kill: Lossless typed canonicalization: canonical structure preserves unit, precision, polarity, scope qualifiers; anything unparseable counts as dissent, not abstention. Round-trip property test on the canonicalizer runs per release; failure blocks deployment.

**V13. Abstention-denominator inflation.** Induce the accurate voters to abstain ("answer only if certain"); agreement is then computed over surviving confident-wrong voters.
Kill: Fixed denominator: agreement = |cluster| / N_roster, abstentions and unparseables counted as non-agreement; additionally require participation ≥ 80% of roster, else verdict is `insufficient-signal`, never `consensus`. Arithmetic.

**V14. Roster stuffing / adaptive selection.** Attacker picks which models to ask after probing who agrees, or pads the panel with near-duplicates until quorum is met by construction.
Kill: Pre-registration: roster, N, k, m, thresholds hash-committed before query issuance; quorum computed only over the committed roster; any additional runs are logged as diagnostics and carry zero quorum weight. Hash comparison.

**V15. Selective reruns (file-drawer).** Re-roll the ensemble until the desired consensus appears; publish that run only.
Kill: Append-only run ledger with monotonic sequence numbers and chained hashes; a published verdict must reference an unbroken ledger segment covering every executed run for that query; gaps/duplicates ⇒ verdict invalid. Chain verification is mechanical.

**V16. Compromised judge.** An LLM judge does the clustering/entailment and is jailbroken or simply shares the voters' blind spots; it certifies unanimity.
Kill: Judge-minimalism: move all aggregation into deterministic code; residual LLM judgments restricted to pairwise entailment, aggregated by majority, and continuously scored against a pinned gold set with hard-coded expected verdicts; any miss ⇒ judge build quarantined. Regression gate.

**V17. Threshold rot.** τ calibrated once; input distribution drifts; yesterday's τ admits today's correlated garbage.
Kill: τ is never hand-set: recomputed each release as a pinned quantile of the null-agreement distribution over the pinned calibration suite (suite hash-versioned). Recompute, don't tune.

## Family 5 — Deep epistemic

**V18. Universal-attractor errors.** Wrong answers that are attractors for anything trained on human text (persistent misconceptions, confident arithmetic slips). Model diversity cannot decorrelate these; the correlation lives in the data distribution.
Kill: Verifier-outranks-consensus: static claim-class → verifier routing table (math → CAS; code → sandboxed test harness; dates/quantities → typed lookup; factuals → hash-verified primary-source citation). Where a deterministic verifier exists, its verdict overrides the vote tally; consensus confidence is granted only over claim classes with no verifier. Routing table + execution.

**V19. Benchmark-contamination echo.** Query (or near-duplicate) sits in pretraining data with a popular wrong answer; all models regurgitate fluently; consensus looks pristine.
Kill: Two deterministic dampeners: (a) hash-screen the query's n-grams against a pinned contamination watchlist; hit ⇒ automatic tier downgrade; (b) parameter-mutation coherence: substitute controlled values (years, names, magnitudes) per a fixed substitution map and require the answer to track the substitutions coherently; memorized echoes typically return stale or incoherent values. Substitution-map diff check.

**V20. Consensus theater on unverifiable claims.** Forecasts, judgments, taste: correlated priors masquerade as fact; no detector can separate these because there is no ground truth to converge on.
Kill: Forced epistemic tagging: output schema stamps every claim `{verifier-backed | multi-lineage-agreed | single-source}` derived mechanically from which gates passed; downstream policy consumes tags, not vibes. Schema validation is deterministic. Honest ceiling: for this class, the deliverable is calibrated labeling, not certainty.

## Family 6 — Insider / own-iron specifics

**V21. Intake selection bias.** Operator routes only flattering questions to the ensemble; consensus quality is irrelevant because the sample is curated.
Kill: Intake registry: every query entering any decision pipeline is hash-logged pre-execution; verdicts are consumable only for registered queries; scheduled reconciliation diffs decisions against the ledger. Diff report.

**V22. Silent config drift.** Weights, prompts, tools, or thresholds swapped mid-stream without notice; historical calibrations silently invalidated.
Kill: Everything hashed at bind time — weights, prompts, tool endpoints, thresholds, suite versions — into a per-run manifest; manifest hash is stamped into the ledger entry; consumers verify manifest against the pinned allowlist before accepting a verdict. Hash equality.

## Irreducible residue

Two things stay probabilistic no matter how many gates you bolt on: (1) shared-corpus priors on claim classes with no deterministic verifier (V18/V19/V20 partially survive grounding, since sources can be scarce, wrong, or mutually copied); (2) novel correlated failure modes not represented in the calibration suite. The engineering answer is not elimination but structure: consensus is demoted from trump to fallback — one evidence stream among several, always subordinate to any available deterministic verifier, always tagged with its provenance class, always auditable end-to-end via the ledger.

## Load-bearing gates (minimum viable stack)

1. Ballot sealing + prompt-hash equality (kills V8, most of V5's leverage).
2. Lineage dedupe: weight-hash + LCA + distinct-class quorum (V1–V3).
3. Corpus commit fence + visibility matrix (V6).
4. Dual-stack tool cross-check (V7).
5. Typed canonicalization + fixed denominator (V11–V13).
6. Pre-registered roster + append-only ledger (V14–V15, V21).
7. Verifier-outranks-consensus routing (V18).
8. Manifest hashing + replay audit (V10, V22).
